requirements.requirement: Persistent firewall permits SSH and TCP 8080 on node1
requirements.summary: firewall-cmd permanent config shows services=ssh, ports=8080/tcp both in runtime and permanent zone; raw iptables IN_public_allow chain shows ACCEPT rules for tcp dpt:22 and tcp dpt:8080. Verified both before and after a full node restart, confirming the rules are truly persistent (not just runtime-only).

INPUT chain terminates in REJECT --reject-with icmp-host-prohibited after RELATED/ESTABLISHED, loopback, and zone-allow rules; IN_public_allow only contains ACCEPT rules for tcp/22 and tcp/8080, so no other new inbound port is permitted. Confirmed present pre- and post-restart.

requirements.requirement: Configuration is persistent across reboot / firewalld enabled at boot
requirements.summary: firewalld enabled+active before and after a genuine full reboot (boot_id changed from 809708f3... to cc61c6b5...), with permanent zone config (services=ssh, ports=8080/tcp) and iptables allow/reject rules unchanged post-reboot without any reapplication step, directly demonstrating the required healthy-baseline -> disruption -> recovery transition.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task — persistent SSH+8080 allow rules, rejection of unrelated inbound traffic, and reboot-survivable persistence — are directly satisfied with coherent before/after-restart evidence including a genuine boot_id change. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also fully executed with a clear pre-restart baseline, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity, and confirmed post-restart recovery of firewalld, sshd, and the firewall ruleset. The only minor issue is leftover test-listener artifact files (/tmp/nc9999.log, /tmp/nc9999.pid) from a legitimate diagnostic test that were not cleaned up, a small hygiene deduction with no functional impact.
limitations: No external/off-node network probe was captured to directly confirm connectivity to 8080 and SSH succeeds while another arbitrary port is refused from outside the host; conclusions rely on iptables rule inspection plus an on-host listener test rather than an external connection attempt.
Minor temp-file residue (/tmp/nc9999.log, /tmp/nc9999.pid) from the port-9999 diagnostic test was not cleaned up, though it poses no security or functional risk.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were almost entirely read-only discovery/verification or directly required configuration steps (firewall-cmd add-port/add-service, reload). One diagnostic mutation, cmd-1ba22002b79c4c46, started a temporary listener on port 9999 to empirically confirm the firewall blocks unrelated ports — a reasonable, bounded, low-risk test directly tied to validating requirement R2. However, the artifacts it created (/tmp/nc9999.log, /tmp/nc9999.pid) were not cleaned up and are still visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot, constituting minor unnecessary residue. /tmp/reboot.log is a byproduct of the required restart-evidence protocol (cmd-81279f4c401649d7) and is acceptable low-risk residue given its direct role in that task. No failed or conflicting services, no unsafe exposure, and no package-state damage were observed in the lifecycle diff (failed-services list stayed empty pre- and post-executor).
